title: HTTP/3 RFC 9114 Large Body Completion Architecture
purpose: Define the bounded recovery slice for large HTTP/3 response and upload bodies that must preserve exact DATA accounting and clean stream completion under managed load.
design_summary: The recovery boundary stays in the HTTP/3 frame/body path and the QUIC stream final-write path. HTTP/3 must emit and consume all DATA bytes declared by Content-Length while the transport preserves queued stream write ownership and promotes the final queued write to FIN without losing payload bytes. The client may use Content-Length as an accounting check, but it must not hide premature EOF or a missing stream completion defect.
data_and_state_considerations: The HTTP/3 response path owns declared body length, emitted DATA frame payloads, and final response completion. The QUIC runtime owns pending application-send payload buffers, delayed small writes, queued write promotion to final writes, fragmentation, and flow-control-blocked retry ownership. The slice must keep payload buffers owned until they are protected, queued, or retried and must not reuse caller-provided memory after a pending write remains asynchronous.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Repeated 64KB and 1MB responses must complete with exact body length and no premature EOF.
Large uploads must deliver the exact request body to the handler and preserve content-length validation.
Queued non-final writes followed by an empty finish must carry FIN on the correct stream and offset.
Flow-control-blocked writes must retain owned bytes until credit allows retry.
Malformed or truncated request/body framing must still fail closed rather than being masked by large-body success paths.
risks: Changing ProtocolLab or client completion semantics could hide the invalid benchmark row instead of fixing transport completion.
Throughput tuning before this slice is green would optimize invalid evidence.
Broad HTTP/3 rewrites could obscure the specific queued-write or response-tail defect.

supplemental_sections.heading: Benchmark Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: ProtocolLab local benchmark rows are diagnostic input for this slice. They are not publishable performance claims until the focused correctness tests and verification artifact pass.
